propositions: Snapshot janitor runs only in the review-bot FastAPI lifespan and does not reclaim snapshots on non-review-bot hosts (developer laptops, CI runners, library embeds), leaving snapshot stores append-only with unbounded growth.

The solution implements an operation-linked GC trigger (mirroring compact_trigger.py) that calls maybe_gc on the gate-resolution tail for attested handles, performing a O(1) stamp stat check without acquiring ticket-store locks or enumerating the store.

When a GC pass is due, a detached child process runs the existing run_gc policy under a stamped worker.lock sidecar and gc flock, with stdio redirected to a log and cwd anchored at the snapshot store root.

The trigger design avoids the long-lock pitfall (bug 0d15-59a4) by holding no ticket-store lock in any branch of the trigger check, never raising into the gate operation, and deferring heavy work to a detached child off the critical path.

Single-flight semantics are enforced via stamped worker.lock adjudication (shared with lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale) and run_gc's existing gc flock; overlap with the review-bot resident janitor is harmless and does not reset the stamp unless run_gc actually ran.
The implementation is operation-linked and in-process with no dependency on CI providers, cron, or daemons; the review-bot resident janitor remains a supplementary cadence.
